title: Stocks Fall On Strong Earnings...What's Breaking?
speaker: David Lin (guest George Noble)

macro_themes.view: Market is starting to separate growth from profitable growth as AI capex crushes free cash flow at Meta, Oracle, CoreWeave.
Rising rates and wider credit spreads create a feedback loop that makes AI infrastructure financing harder.
AI may succeed technologically while the companies funding the build-out fail to earn returns for shareholders.

calls.reason: George Noble: debt ballooning, ROIC below cost of capital, bonds yielding 15-16%; retail buying the dip is not how bottoms form. His biggest short, doubled recently.
calls.quote: We actually doubled the short a couple of weeks ago. It's it's our biggest position. I think there's a very good chance CoreWeave goes bankrupt.

calls.reason: Noble: robotics venture worth $30-40B against a ~$1.5T market cap; operating margin 2.6%; 'the product is the stock'.
calls.quote: in the case of Tesla, the product is the stock... it's all just designed to try and jack up the stock price

notes: Mostly an explainer on Meta/Tesla/CoreWeave/Oracle financials; Meta and Oracle discussed without a directional call. Tesla bearish is implied from Noble's valuation skepticism, not an explicit trade.
